On the day of misedashi or erikae, a new maiko or geiko visits all of the ochaya in her district to ask for their support. This is called aisatsumawari ("making rounds","calling on"). It is a busy day, so the geiko or maiko only drops in super quickly.

The following day, the new geiko or maiko makes those rounds again. Called oreimawari ("making rounds of gratitude"), I think it is humbler and more intimate because the new geiko or maiko is dressed casually, without oshiroi.
